minutes.headline: Water District heard a developer's plan to expand the district for a Barber Street subdivision; no vote, residents voiced concerns.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was a discussion with a developer seeking to extend the water district boundary to a Barber/Bird Street property with contamination history, plus residents' questions about petition, vote and development. The board then discussed the FY23-24 budget salary line pending hiring, possible warrant articles (vehicles, lead line replacement, Mass Ave amendment), rate feedback and a costly test boring change order. Only a motion to adjourn was made.

public_comment.topic: Developer (stated name James Hall, of Holbrook) presented plan to bring water to a Barber Street property, at least 25 single-family or 55+ homes.
Neighbor across the street with a contaminated well asked where the pipe would go and about the developer's experience with DEP contamination rules.
Resident living on Arbor Street asked about the map and loop of water lines.
Resident asked how petition signers and district voters can make an informed decision without information on the development.
Resident asked about the petition requirement and what passing the petition means.
Sister of the property owners described heavy spending on contamination work and ongoing testing costs, supporting water to solve the problem.

what_happened.line: No vote was taken; the only motion was to adjourn, so the board decided nothing by vote at this meeting.
A developer asked the district to extend its boundary to a Barber Street property for at least 25 single-family or 55+ homes.
Any expansion would go to a special meeting once the developer gathers signatures, not the March meeting.
The board deferred the salary line for FY23-24 until hiring is complete, with the budget to be settled at the next meeting.
Warrant articles on vehicles, lead line replacement and a Mass Ave amendment are to be drafted for a vote in two weeks; the Explorer replacement is left out.

why_it_matters: A boundary expansion would be put to district voters at a special meeting, and the warrant articles on lead line replacement and the Mass Ave appropriation would affect district spending and water rates.

A special meeting on the boundary expansion, if the developer gathers the required signatures.
